risksForTheArchitect: R1 — the shipped repeat rule is containment, where the approved spec v11 says 'compared whole'. I drove it and it loses no word: `strings.Contains(w.text, piece)` (packages/envoy/internal/contracts/normalize.go:1139) can drop only a character sequence the delivered text already holds, so every word still reaches the agent and only the label-to-value adjacency changes. In the attachment alert I posted, the field value `web-3` was dropped because the `fallback` line already carried it, leaving `Host` with its value one line above rather than beside it. The architect's decision of 2026-10-25T03:14:47Z is on record and the CHANGELOG and the controller reference both describe containment, so the shipped words and the behaviour agree; the approved spec's words do not. Whether that needs a note on the issue is the architect's call.

R2 — the CHANGELOG and the PR body claim a message composed in a Slack client 'reads as it did'. That holds only while every rich_text leaf string is a substring of the message's own `text`. Slack escapes `&`, `<` and `>` as HTML entities in a message's text object (docs.slack.dev/messaging/formatting-message-text, 'Escaping text'), and a rich_text element is not a text object, so a message containing one of those three characters typed literally — 'p99 > 500ms', 'build & deploy' — would carry the raw character in the block and the entity in `text`, and the block copy would be delivered as a second line. I drove that shape on the listener and saw exactly that: `<@U0LEGION> build & deploy failed\n build & deploy failed`. The premise is unproven, not disproven: the repository holds no captured Slack body (the planner records this as gap-analysis finding F1) and I could not read one back, so I have modelled the body rather than observed Slack sending it. If the architect wants it closed rather than carried, the narrow fix is to compare a piece against the text with Slack's three entities applied as well as plainly.

R3 — the delivered order inside one object is Slack's display order only for the seven string fields. Descent into an object's non-string values is alphabetical by key (normalize.go:1172), so a Block Kit section's `fields` are delivered before the section's own `text`, and a button's hidden `value` before its label — I observed `*Service*
api
*Env*
production
*p99* is 3.2s …` and `ack:alert-77
Acknowledge`. Every word is present; the order differs from what Slack renders. The plan's recorded departure says the order inside one object is Slack's display order, which is true of the seven fields and not of the nested descent.
